report.incidentSummary: Incident INC-6097 involved a SEV1 drop in OTP login success rates down to ~70% starting around 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC) on 2026-10-16. Investigation confirmed that internal services, databases, caches, and notification-service API calls to the external SMS provider were operating normally, with SMS requests accepted (status 202). The root cause is external SMS provider delivery degradation/failure preventing users from receiving OTP codes.
report.rootCauseStatement: External SMS provider delivery degradation/failure, where OTP dispatch requests were successfully accepted (status 202) by the provider but messages failed to reach end-users.

hypotheses.cause: External SMS provider delivery failure or routing degradation causing OTP messages not to reach end-users.
hypotheses.rationale: OTP success rate dropped sharply while internal services, database, cache, and notification-service API submissions (status 202) remained completely healthy and normal.

hypotheses.cause: Code or configuration regression in auth-service.
hypotheses.rationale: No code changes or deployments occurred on auth-service; internal dependencies and resource utilization were fully healthy.

facts.statement: Auth-service otp_success_rate dropped from ~97% to ~70% starting at 2026-10-16T05:10Z (10:40 IST).

No code deployments or configuration changes occurred on auth-service or notification-service during the investigation window; the only change on auth-service was an infrastructure log-shipper agent upgrade (CHG-48221) at 04:54Z.
Notification-service logs show SMS requests being successfully accepted by the external SMS provider with status 202.
Database and cache metrics remained completely normal with low latency and high cache hit rates throughout the window.
Past incidents PIR-2004 and PIR-1602 describe identical symptoms where SMS provider degradation or outage caused OTP success rates to drop because users did not receive SMS messages.

inferences.statement: Because notification-service API calls returned status 202 Accepted but OTP verification success dropped, the bottleneck is downstream in the external SMS provider's ability to deliver messages to telecom operators/users.

Auth-service otp_success_rate begins dropping sharply from ~97% down to ~70% (approx 10:40 IST).
Incident INC-6097 reported by On-call SRE at 11:20 IST (05:50 UTC).

confidence.rationale: Auth-service OTP success rate dropped to ~70% at 05:10Z without any internal service errors, database/cache bottlenecks, or code deployments. Notification-service successfully submits SMS to the external SMS provider (status 202), matching patterns from past external SMS provider incidents (PIR-2004, PIR-1602).

gaps.description: Lack of direct visibility into internal metrics of the external SMS provider (blackbox dependency).

recommendedActions.action: Trigger failover to secondary SMS provider if primary provider recovery is delayed (as done in PIR-2004).
recommendedActions.rationale: Ensures immediate restoration of high OTP delivery and login success rates.

payload.markdown:
# Investigation report: OTP logins failing

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** completed · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** baseline agent

## Summary
Incident INC-6097 involved a SEV1 drop in OTP login success rates down to ~70% starting around 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC) on 2026-10-16. Investigation confirmed that internal services, databases, caches, and notification-service API calls to the external SMS provider were operating normally, with SMS requests accepted (status 202). The root cause is external SMS provider delivery degradation/failure preventing users from receiving OTP codes.

**Root cause:** External SMS provider delivery degradation/failure, where OTP dispatch requests were successfully accepted (status 202) by the provider but messages failed to reach end-users.

## Hypotheses
1. **External SMS provider delivery failure or routing degradation causing OTP messages not to reach end-users.** — `sms-provider`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_3, ev_8, ev_12, ev_26] · Contradicting: none
   - OTP success rate dropped sharply while internal services, database, cache, and notification-service API submissions (status 202) remained completely healthy and normal.
2. **Code or configuration regression in auth-service.** — `auth-service`, deployment_regression, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: none · Contradicting: [ev_5, ev_14, ev_15, ev_16, ev_17, ev_20]
   - No code changes or deployments occurred on auth-service; internal dependencies and resource utilization were fully healthy.

## Facts
- Auth-service otp_success_rate dropped from ~97% to ~70% starting at 2026-10-16T05:10Z (10:40 IST). [ev_3]
- No code deployments or configuration changes occurred on auth-service or notification-service during the investigation window; the only change on auth-service was an infrastructure log-shipper agent upgrade (CHG-48221) at 04:54Z. [ev_5, ev_20]
- Notification-service logs show SMS requests being successfully accepted by the external SMS provider with status 202. [ev_8, ev_26]
- Database and cache metrics remained completely normal with low latency and high cache hit rates throughout the window. [ev_14, ev_15, ev_16, ev_17]
- Past incidents PIR-2004 and PIR-1602 describe identical symptoms where SMS provider degradation or outage caused OTP success rates to drop because users did not receive SMS messages. [ev_12]

## Inferences
- Because notification-service API calls returned status 202 Accepted but OTP verification success dropped, the bottleneck is downstream in the external SMS provider's ability to deliver messages to telecom operators/users. [ev_3, ev_8, ev_12]

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16T04:54:00.000Z** Infrastructure log-shipper agent upgraded on auth-service node pool (CHG-48221). [ev_5, ev_20]
- **2026-10-16T05:10:00.000Z** Auth-service otp_success_rate begins dropping sharply from ~97% down to ~70% (approx 10:40 IST). [ev_3]
- **2026-10-16T05:50:00.000Z** Incident INC-6097 reported by On-call SRE at 11:20 IST (05:50 UTC). [ev_3]

## Confidence
0.95: Auth-service OTP success rate dropped to ~70% at 05:10Z without any internal service errors, database/cache bottlenecks, or code deployments. Notification-service successfully submits SMS to the external SMS provider (status 202), matching patterns from past external SMS provider incidents (PIR-2004, PIR-1602).

## Gaps
- Lack of direct visibility into internal metrics of the external SMS provider (blackbox dependency). (impact: Prevents direct identification of whether the issue is at carrier interconnects or SMS provider infrastructure.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Escalate to the external SMS provider support team regarding SMS delivery failures and delays. [ev_3, ev_8, ev_12]
  - Why: Provider is accepting requests with 202 but failing to deliver messages to users.
  - Verify: Verify delivery success rates and operator delivery reports with the provider.
- **[next]** Trigger failover to secondary SMS provider if primary provider recovery is delayed (as done in PIR-2004). [ev_12]
  - Why: Ensures immediate restoration of high OTP delivery and login success rates.
  - Verify: Monitor auth-service otp_success_rate metric returning to ~97%.
